recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit. The seed issue is already correctly represented in the current Security and Privacy module, and additional prose would be redundant rather than a necessary reconciliation fix.
issue_request: FHIR-10581 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution asking the Privacy and Security module to add an H4 section titled De-Identification, pseudonymization, anonymization. The requested section was to emphasize that de-identification is a process, include an access-control obligation use case, discuss Observation direct and indirect identifiers including specimen pseudonymization, and point to external ISO, NIST, IHE, and DICOM standards.
initial_application: The historical application is commit f72fd6237875c6ba9d2a21e235881c7fed559700, whose message explicitly says the Security and Privacy module was updated for GF#10581 to speak to de-identification. That commit added the requested H4 and the core process, use-case, Observation, and external-standard guidance to source/secpriv-module.html.
additional_context: FHIR-14312 is a later Published/Persuasive same-section issue implemented by 56b668e7bc4866d19adfd2627cf2aae60f564035. It refined the FHIR-10581 section by correcting wording and adding narrative, attachment, ids, identifiers, and risk guidance. The linked 2016 Zulip thread supports the current framing that de-identification is a process and that references, direct identifiers, indirect identifiers, quasi-identifiers, and narrative/text are difficult to classify safely. No direct Confluence references or conflicting community evidence were found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source/secpriv-module.html contains the de-identification H4, process-not-algorithm framing, access-control obligation trigger, Observation identifier examples, security-label note, and links to ISO/IEC 20889, ISO/TS 25237, NIST IR 8053, the IHE De-Identification Handbook, and DICOM Part 15. The page is linked from current module navigation source, confirming it is current specification source rather than a stale artifact.
